briefing.text: Which matrix to pseudobulk. The library reports that in this AnnData .X holds log-normalised floats, layers['scaled'] holds scaled values, and only layers['scvi_counts'] looks like raw integer UMI counts (PopV stores raw counts there). Verify this yourself before relying on it: the matrix you aggregate must be non-negative integers (np.allclose(data, np.round(data)), max well above 10) and its per-cell sums should match obs nCount_RNA / n_counts. Summing or averaging log-normalised values and feeding them to DESeq2/edgeR gives compressed, pseudocount-distorted log2FCs. Aggregate the raw-count layer by SUM (not mean) per sample x cell type and fit the count model on those sums.
briefing.reason: Using .X or the scaled layer instead of raw counts changes every reported log2FC; the count layer is not in the default slot, so a team starting from the data alone could easily aggregate the wrong matrix.

briefing.text: The log2FC must come from a model fitted on a samples x genes pseudobulk count table, not from a per-cell test. The library reports 4 samples x 2 monocyte types, so at most 8 pseudobulk columns. Scanpy rank_genes_groups 'logfoldchanges' is log2((expm1(mean log1p)+1e-9)/(...)) and Seurat adds a +1 pseudocount; both can differ by several log2 units from a count-based pseudobulk log2FC for sparse genes, and cells are pseudoreplicates of the sample. The library also notes uns['log1p'] is an empty dict in this file, so rank_genes_groups can raise KeyError 'base'. Use pseudobulk DESeq2/PyDESeq2 (or edgeR) and take log2FoldChange from that fit.
briefing.reason: The task asks for pseudobulk DE; a cell-level shortcut gives numerically different fold changes, especially for markers that are sparse in one subset.

briefing.text: Fit the model only on the two monocyte groups. The library reports the file has about 18 annotated PBMC cell types. If all sample x cell-type pseudobulks go into one DESeq2 fit, the size factors (median of ratios against an all-sample geometric mean), dispersion estimates and gene filter are driven by T, B and NK cells and the monocyte log2FCs change. Subset to classical and non-classical monocytes before aggregation and fitting, and confirm the count table given to the DE tool has only those pseudobulks (at most 8 columns) with size factors estimated on those columns only. An all-cell-type fit is at most a sensitivity check.
briefing.reason: Whether other cell types are in the fit changes normalisation and therefore the log2FC values that get reported.

briefing.text: Choice of cell-type label column. The library reports obs has several PopV label columns: popv_prediction (final ontology-aware consensus), popv_majority_vote_prediction, and per-method columns (celltypist, scanvi, knn_on_scvi, svm, xgboost, onclass), which need not agree; popv_prediction_score / popv_majority_vote_score count how many methods agree. The label set has only 'classical monocyte' and 'non-classical monocyte', so intermediate (CD14++CD16+) monocytes, DC-like cells and doublets are forced into one of the two groups, which dilutes marker fold changes. Check: crosstab popv_prediction against popv_majority_vote_prediction for the two monocyte labels, count cells per label per sample, and look at the score distribution within each label. The library's recommendation is popv_prediction as the primary grouping (PopV's documented final call), with a re-run restricted to high-agreement cells as a sensitivity; if the columns give materially different LFCs, say so rather than choosing silently.
briefing.reason: Which column defines the two groups decides which cells are in each pseudobulk; different columns can give different fold changes and the file offers several plausible ones.

briefing.text: The two groups are paired. The library reports both monocyte subsets come from the same 4 samples (obs 'sample': sample1-4). A design of ~ celltype treats sample differences as noise, while ~ sample + celltype blocks on sample; the two give somewhat different log2FCs and very different dispersions/p-values. Check: tabulate cells per sample x cell type, confirm each sample contributes both subsets, run both designs and compare the 8 target-gene LFCs. The library's recommendation (its judgement from standard practice; the task text does not name a design) is the paired design ~ sample + celltype as primary when every sample has both subsets; if a sample lacks one subset, drop that sample or fall back to ~ celltype, and state which was used.
briefing.reason: The design formula is a free choice the task does not fix and it shifts the reported log2FCs; teams should make it deliberately and know how much the 8 values move between designs.

briefing.text: Guard against a sign flip. The task wants log2(non-classical / classical). PyDESeq2 contrast is [factor, tested_level, ref_level] and reports tested/ref; DESeq2 in R uses the alphabetically first level as reference unless relevelled ('classical monocyte' sorts before 'non-classical monocyte', which happens to give the wanted direction, but do not rely on it). Set the contrast explicitly as [celltype, non-classical, classical]. After fitting, for 2-3 genes compute a crude log2 ratio of summed CPM (non-classical over classical) straight from the pseudobulk counts and confirm it has the same sign as the model log2FoldChange. Renaming the two levels to simple tokens without spaces or hyphens before building the design avoids formula/level-name parsing problems (this renaming advice is precautionary, not confirmed by a source).
briefing.reason: A reversed contrast negates all eight answers; the level names contain spaces and a hyphen, which is where such errors and parsing failures arise.

briefing.text: Shrunken versus maximum-likelihood log2FC. lfcShrink / PyDESeq2 lfc_shrink (apeglm) overwrites results_df and pulls LFCs toward zero, strongly for genes with low or zero counts in one group; with only 4 samples per group shrunken and MLE values can differ by more than a log2 unit for genes nearly absent in one subset. PyDESeq2 lfc_shrink has also had a reported bug changing LFC magnitude or sign for some genes. Conversely, the MLE for a gene with all-zero counts in one group is large and unstable. Check: record both MLE and shrunken LFC for the 8 genes and list each gene's raw pseudobulk counts in every sample to see whether any group is at or near zero. The library's recommendation is to report the unshrunken MLE log2FoldChange from the standard results table as the default 'log2FC' (what a plain DE run returns), give the shrunken value as a sensitivity, and flag any gene whose value depends on near-zero counts. Do not mix shrunken and unshrunken values across genes.
briefing.reason: Several target genes are subset-specific markers that may be near zero in the other group, exactly where shrinkage changes the number most; teams need to know which estimate they are reporting.

briefing.text: Default filters can silently remove samples or target genes. Non-classical monocytes are a small population, so a sample may contribute few cells. decoupler get_pseudobulk defaults (min_cells=10, min_counts=1000) drop small pseudobulks without error, which unbalances a paired design; expression filters (filter_by_expr min_count=10, min_total_count=15, or an 'at least 10 counts in N samples' rule) can drop a marker gene that is near zero in one subset, giving NaN or missing LFC. Check: print cells and total counts per sample x cell type before and after aggregation, confirm all expected pseudobulks survive, and confirm all 8 target genes (FCGR3A, CX3CR1, CDKN1C, MS4A7, CD14, S100A8, S100A9, VCAN) are in var_names and in the fitted table. State the thresholds used; do not let a filter remove a requested gene (relax the gene filter or filter on the union across groups); if a pseudobulk has very few cells, report the result with and without that sample.
briefing.reason: A dropped pseudobulk changes the fit and a dropped gene leaves a required answer field empty; both happen without an error message under common defaults.

briefing.text: Composition bias when comparing two different cell types. Hand-computed log2 ratios of CPM (library-size scaling) are biased when a few very highly expressed genes differ strongly between groups, which is typical between monocyte subsets (a handful of abundant genes take a large share of the classical-monocyte library), shifting every other gene's CPM. DESeq2 median-of-ratios and edgeR TMM correct for this but assume most genes are not differentially expressed. Check: compare DESeq2 size factors (or TMM norm factors) with plain library-size ratios across the pseudobulks; if they diverge by cell type, CPM-based LFCs are shifted by about log2 of that divergence. Take the reported LFCs from the median-of-ratios/TMM-normalised model, and use raw CPM ratios only as a sign/sanity check.
briefing.reason: It tells teams not to report a hand-computed CPM ratio as the answer, and explains why the CPM sanity check suggested for the sign may differ in magnitude from the model value without indicating an error.

shared_assumptions: Both teams took the obs column popv_prediction as the definition of the two groups and kept every cell carrying either label (1329 classical, 368 non-classical), including low-agreement cells and cells whose Seurat cluster disagrees with their label. Neither tested the label against the unsupervised clustering stored in the same file.

Both assumed a paired design (~ sample + celltype) with the four 'sample' values as independent biological replicates. The file gives no donor or condition metadata beyond the names sample1-sample4, so the pairing is an assumption about the experiment, not something read from the data.

Both assumed the reported number should be the unshrunken maximum-likelihood coefficient of a DESeq2-style negative binomial GLM. Neither could run a real DESeq2 package (I confirmed none is installed and none can be downloaded), and neither validated its hand-written fit against an input with a known answer; the two reimplementations agreeing with each other to about 0.05 is the only cross-check.
Both estimated size factors by median of ratios; team A states this was on the 8 monocyte pseudobulks only with no gene filter, team B does not state which columns or genes entered the calculation.

Both summed the layer scvi_counts. This one I checked structurally and it holds: the layer is all integers, its row sums equal obs n_counts, and its per-gene means equal var vst.mean (the Seurat raw-count mean) for every gene, so it is the original count matrix.
unused_evidence: obs seurat_clusters / RNA_snn_res.1 (20 unsupervised clusters). Crosstab with popv_prediction: cluster 2 holds 1229 classical and 6 non-classical-labelled cells; cluster 11 holds 361 non-classical and 12 classical-labelled cells; cluster 15 holds 81 classical-labelled cells mixed with T-cell labels (possible doublets). Neither team used these columns. Because the classical markers are tens of times lower in non-classical cells, a handful of classical-like cells inside the non-classical label can supply a large share of that group's VCAN/CD14/S100A8/S100A9 counts.

obs popv_prediction_score / popv_majority_vote_score (number of agreeing methods, 2-6). Team A used it once as a sensitivity (score >= 5) and saw VCAN move by 0.43 and CD14 by 0.35; team B did not use it. 113 of the 1697 monocyte-labelled cells have score < 6.

obs popv_parent (ontology parent call: 1292 classical, 362 non-classical, 81 'mononuclear cell') and the six per-method prediction columns with probabilities: unused by both, another way to mark boundary cells.

var vst.mean / vst.variance (Seurat statistics on the raw counts): unused by both; they confirm the layer is raw counts (see above). Top genes are MALAT1, mitochondrial genes, NEAT1, ARHGAP15, RIPOR2, and S100A8/S100A9/LYZ are low overall, so the low S100A8 that team A flagged is a property of the assay, not a damaged layer. Team A's note that the layer maximum is 99 is wrong for the whole matrix (maximum is 190).
layers['scaled'] and obsm embeddings: unused; not relevant to a count-based pseudobulk fit.

Pseudobulks of the other 16 cell types in the same samples: unused. They would matter only under a reading in which size factors or dispersions are estimated on all cell types, and they give an ambient-RNA floor for the classical markers (the library raised this; neither team reports having looked).
unresolved_weak_points: Team A: 'DESeq2 is reimplemented' - reported, not resolved. It was compared only with CPM ratios (within 0.25), which is a sign check, not a validation of the fit. The dependence of each coefficient on the dispersion value was asserted ('MLE LFCs depend little on dispersion') but not measured, although pseudobulk sizes range from 80 to 507 cells so size factors differ several-fold.
Team A: 'S100A8 rests on very low non-classical counts (1-5 per pseudobulk)' - reported only. No standard error, no leave-one-sample-out, no statement of how far the value could move.

Team A: the high-agreement sensitivity moved VCAN by 0.43 and CD14 by 0.35 - reported as a sensitivity only. Its own plan said to change method if LFCs differ materially across labels; it did not say why 0.43 is not material, nor which cells cause the shift.

Team B: 'not real DESeq2, values may differ by 0.1-0.3 for CX3CR1/CDKN1C/VCAN' - reported only. Dispersion is moment-estimated; no sweep over dispersion values and no known-answer test. Team B's pitfalls_checked list is empty and it ran no high-agreement or cluster-based label sensitivity.
second_readings: Design: 'pseudobulk DE comparing A vs B' can be fitted as ~ celltype (samples as unpaired replicates) or ~ sample + celltype (paired). Team A measured a difference under 0.12; team B did not fit the unpaired NB model.
Which log2FC: the default results-table value (unshrunken MLE) or a shrunken estimate. Shrinkage would matter most for the genes with near-zero counts in one group (S100A8, CDKN1C, FCGR3A, VCAN).

'Calculate log2 fold change as (non-classical) / (classical)' can be read literally as the log2 ratio of normalised pseudobulk expression rather than a GLM coefficient; the teams found these differ from the model value by up to about 0.2-0.25.
Normalisation universe: size factors from the two monocyte groups only, or from all sample x cell-type pseudobulks in the file.

Group definition: popv_prediction as given, the majority-vote column, or labels cleaned of boundary/low-agreement cells. The direction of the ratio is not in doubt (both teams checked the sign against raw ratios).
challenge.verdict: Moderately high trust in direction and size: two different hand-written NB fits agree to about 0.05 on all eight genes, the signs were checked against raw ratios, and I confirmed the count layer is the original raw matrix (its gene means equal var vst.mean). The values are not yet pinned to better than a few tenths for the classical markers: neither team ran a real DESeq2 or validated its own fit, VCAN and CD14 moved by 0.35-0.43 when a few percent of low-agreement cells were dropped, and the paired-versus-unpaired and shrunken-versus-unshrunken readings were not closed.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your high-agreement run moved VCAN by 0.43 and CD14 by 0.35, yet it removes only about 5-7% of the cells in each group, and your plan said to change method if LFCs differ materially across labels. You have not used obs seurat_clusters. Crosstab popv_prediction against seurat_clusters for the two monocyte labels, list the non-classical-labelled cells that sit in the classical-dominated cluster or have popv_prediction_score < 6, and compute per sample what share of the non-classical pseudobulk counts of VCAN, CD14, S100A8 and S100A9 those cells contribute. Is the shift caused by a handful of cells? What in the task text or the data decides whether those cells belong in the group, and does the result change your method or only your stated uncertainty?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your weakest point is the hand-written DESeq2, and it has been compared only with CPM ratios. Run two checks on de.py: (1) a known-answer test, e.g. an input with equal size factors, or the zero-dispersion (Poisson) limit, where the celltype coefficient has a closed form you can compute by hand; (2) refit the 8 genes with the dispersion fixed at several values across a wide range (including your gene-wise, trend and MAP values) and report the range of each coefficient, given that your pseudobulks hold 80 to 507 cells and so have very different size factors. Is every one of the 8 values stable under these checks? Does the result change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: you list 'shrunken vs MLE LFC' as not found in the data, while also reporting that S100A8 has 1-5 counts per non-classical pseudobulk. Print the 8 x 8 table of raw pseudobulk counts for the eight genes, mark every entry below 10 and any zero, and give the standard error of each MLE coefficient plus a leave-one-sample-out range. For the genes resting on small counts, how far does the value move between the unshrunken coefficient, a shrunken estimate and a leave-one-out fit? Which of these does the task's phrase 'report the log2FC' after 'running DE analysis' point to, and does the result change your method? (For your records: the layer's maximum over all cells is 190, not 99, and its per-gene means equal var vst.mean exactly, so the layer is the original raw counts.)

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the task says only 'pseudobulk differential expression' and the file describes the replicates only as sample1-sample4. Build one table of the 8 values under each reasonable reading you can fit: ~ sample + celltype, ~ celltype, size factors estimated on all sample x cell-type pseudobulks instead of the 8 monocyte columns, and with a usual low-count gene filter applied before size-factor estimation. Report the largest spread per gene and which reading causes it. Is any gene's spread larger than the uncertainty you are prepared to state, and does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your only label check was popv_prediction against the majority-vote column, and you used neither obs popv_prediction_score nor obs seurat_clusters. The other team found that dropping low-agreement cells, about 5-7% of each group, moved two of the classical-marker values by 0.35 to 0.43. Crosstab popv_prediction against seurat_clusters for the two monocyte labels, list the non-classical-labelled cells that sit in the classical-dominated cluster or have popv_prediction_score < 6, and compute per sample what share of the non-classical pseudobulk counts of VCAN, CD14, S100A8 and S100A9 those cells contribute. Your plan said to change method if label choice moves the LFC a lot: does this result trigger that rule, and what in the task text or the data decides whether those cells belong in the group?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: you named the moment-estimated dispersion as your weakest point and expected differences of 0.1-0.3 for CX3CR1, CDKN1C and VCAN, but did not measure it. Run two checks on de.py: (1) a known-answer test, e.g. an input with equal size factors, or the zero-dispersion (Poisson) limit, where the celltype coefficient has a closed form you can compute by hand; (2) refit the 8 genes with the dispersion fixed at several values across a wide range and report the range of each coefficient, given that your pseudobulks hold 80 to 507 cells and so have very different size factors. Is every one of the 8 values stable, or does your 0.1-0.3 estimate stand? Does the result change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your method note does not say which pseudobulk columns and which genes entered the median-of-ratios size factors, and you did not fit an unpaired negative binomial model. State exactly what was used (the 8 monocyte pseudobulks only, or all sample x cell-type pseudobulks; any gene filter), then build one table of the 8 values under each reasonable reading you can fit: ~ sample + celltype, ~ celltype, size factors on all cell types versus monocytes only, and with a usual low-count gene filter. The file describes the replicates only as sample1-sample4. Report the largest spread per gene and which reading causes it. Does it change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: several of the eight genes are expected to be near zero in one of the two groups, and the other team found single-digit counts per non-classical pseudobulk for one of them. Print the 8 x 8 table of raw pseudobulk counts for the eight genes, mark every entry below 10 and any zero, and give the standard error of each coefficient plus a leave-one-sample-out range. For the genes resting on small counts, how far does the value move between the unshrunken coefficient, a shrunken estimate and a leave-one-out fit? Which of these does the task's phrase 'report the log2FC' after 'running DE analysis' point to, and does the result change your method?

In DESeq2 and in PyDESeq2, is the log2FoldChange in the default results table the unshrunken maximum-likelihood coefficient, which dispersion value (gene-wise, trend or final MAP) is used in the GLM fit that produces it, and with four replicates per group can outlier replacement, Cook's-distance handling or independent filtering change the reported log2FoldChange (as opposed to the p-value)?
questions.why: Both teams wrote their own DESeq2-style fit because no package was installed, with different dispersion estimators. Knowing exactly what the standard tool reports by default tells them what their reimplementation must match and whether shrinkage is part of a default run.
reasons: a number within 1 percent of another team's value for "S100A9_log2FC"

questions.question: In widely used pseudobulk tutorials for single-cell RNA-seq (the decoupler plus PyDESeq2 workflow and the DESeq2-based pseudobulk workflow), when two cell types taken from the same samples are compared, is the design formula normally the cell-type factor alone or sample plus cell type, and what default minimum-cell, minimum-count and gene-expression filters are applied before the fit?
questions.why: The task says only 'pseudobulk differential expression'. Paired versus unpaired design and default filters are the main method choices that move the fold changes of low-count genes, and neither team showed what a standard run does.
reasons: a number within 1 percent of another team's value for "S100A9_log2FC"

questions.question: How do DESeq2 and PyDESeq2 compute median-of-ratios size factors by default: which genes enter the calculation (only genes with non-zero counts in every sample?), is any pre-filter applied, and how much can the size factors of two cell-type groups change when pseudobulks of many other, unrelated cell types are included in the same dataset object?
questions.why: One team did not state which pseudobulks and genes entered its size factors, and a constant shift in size factors between the two groups shifts all eight log2 fold changes by the same amount.
reasons: a number within 1 percent of another team's value for "S100A9_log2FC"
